judgments.reasoning_cat1: The numerator is "all Obligations of Borrower" while the denominator, Tangible Net Worth, is defined by reference to Fund alone, so the ratio mixes two different measuring entities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.16(b) caps this ratio at 0.9%, which against the $600,000,000 Tangible Net Worth floor permits roughly $5.4 million of Obligations — impossible to reconcile with the $50,000,000 Maximum Revolver Amount and Section 2.1(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A named corporation; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "Subsidiary" proviso expressly excludes Bar-K, yet "Change of Control" clause (c) requires Permitted Holders to own 100% of Servicer's Stock — Servicer is treated as both inside and outside the credit group.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names the parties and subject matter; the singular "Borrower" where two Borrowers exist is a small looseness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a Loan Document and a Section 3.1(b)(iv) closing condition, and Sections 4.8, 8.15 and 9.1(e)/(o) all depend on it; consistent in substance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The alternative branch — "any settlement agent (including a title company, title agency, attorney or law firm) covered by a Closing Protection Letter" — is a general category qualified by a list, and the escrow-instruction condition is embedded rather than separately stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 2.2(b), 3.1(t)(iv) and 6.18 rely on the term; the Approved Title Insurance Company definition supplies the letter, so the structure holds together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare balance-sheet test ("assets greater than… debts") stated "at fair valuations," omitting the usual unreasonably-small-capital and ability-to-pay prongs; the truncation is itself a construction question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.12(a) represents Solvency and Section 5.12(b) separately addresses fraudulent transfer intent, and Eligible Notes Receivable clause (q) applies the test to makers; no direct conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It sweeps options, warrants and "other equivalents (regardless of how designated)" into "Stock," so a test phrased as owning "100% of the Stock" becomes hard to satisfy or apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Change of Control" clauses (b)-(d) demand ownership of 100% of the Stock of Manager, Servicer and each Subsidiary, and Restricted Payments clause (c) separately addresses warrants and options — the breadth of this definition strains those tests.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (a) is confined to "unsecured Indebtedness," which is a clear limit but an odd one given clause (b).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "Subordinated Note" definition describes notes evidencing Approved Debt as "secured by the assets of Fund," and Permitted Liens clause (c) allows liens for Approved Debt, so secured paper counts as Subordinated Debt through clause (b) despite clause (a)'s unsecured requirement; Tangible Net Worth then adds Subordinated Debt back to equity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cap is defined by a long parenthetical accounting formula that expressly leaves the treatment of unrealised gains and losses "in Manager's discretion," so the permitted principal amount is not objectively ascertainable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It describes the note as "secured by the assets of Fund," which sits against the "Subordinated Debt" requirement of unsecured Indebtedness and against Section 7.2's negative pledge except for Permitted Liens.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two clearly differentiated forms with specified signatories; "satisfactory to Lender" is the only soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Permitted Reorganization clause (b), Section 7.7(b) and Section 7.10(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso excludes from "Subsidiary" any entity formed after the Closing Date that is not funded with Borrower assets, any New Fund, and Bar-K — a set of carve-outs broad enough to swallow the general rule, and "capitalized or otherwise funded with assets of such Borrower" is itself vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.13 forbids forming or acquiring "any Subsidiary" without Lender's consent, but the proviso means most newly formed entities are simply not Subsidiaries, so the covenant and the whole raft of "and its Subsidiaries" obligations can be sidestepped.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tracks the UCC concept with an enumerated list of supported obligations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Borrower Collateral clause (j).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A formula, but the connector between the two halves is garbled in this text and the definition adds Subordinated Debt back into equity — an unusual construction that could be read either way if the operator were in doubt.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the denominator of the Senior Leverage Ratio and the subject of Section 7.16(a)'s $600,000,000 floor and Section 3.1(n)'s closing condition; the interaction with the 0.9% ratio cap produces an impossible result.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing words "attributable to the taxable income or gain of such Borrower" have no clear antecedent, since the distributing entity was described as "Fund or Manager" and the recipients as "holders of its Stock".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.10(a)(i) permits Tax Distributions subject to delivery of quarterly financials; consistent in structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure pointer definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.5 does define "Taxes"; accurate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (a) says a Triggering Event exists if "an Event of Default has occurred," with no requirement that it be continuing or uncured — a once-and-forever trigger on the face of the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(b) then conditions reserves on a Triggering Event having "occurred and is continuing," which the definition does not accommodate; the $500,000,000 portfolio test in clause (b) also sits oddly with the $600,000,000 net worth covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Trivially definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in structure; content left to a form satisfactory to Lender.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1(b)(iii) requires delivery and Section 8.12 makes termination a default; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of five named individuals.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure pointer definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A named bank; entirely definite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence redefines "Borrower" for financial covenants to mean Fund and its Subsidiaries consolidated "unless the context clearly requires otherwise" — an escape hatch with no ascertainable boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It collides with the "Borrower" definition ("each of and either of Fund and Manager") and with the Senior Leverage Ratio, which measures Obligations of "Borrower" against Fund-only Tangible Net Worth.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear tie-breaker rule preferring Article 9 definitions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the "Code" definition's own multi-jurisdiction proviso and with Section 4.7's reference to Sections 8-106 and 9-104 et seq.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It legislates that "including" is non-limiting and "or" means "and/or," which displaces the ordinary interpretive canons and is itself a frequent battleground where lists are involved.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with Section 16.2 (headings) and Section 16.3 (no construction against either party) and applies to the many enumerated lists in this document, notably "Borrower Collateral" and "Loan Documents".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence incorporating attached schedules and exhibits; the qualifier "attached" is the only limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit B-2 (the Borrowing Base Certificate) is not in fact attached — it reads "[form to be provided by Lender]" — so an incorporated exhibit central to Section 3.3(f) has no content.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean "lesser of" formula between two defined amounts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The $50,000,000 ceiling cannot be squared with Section 7.16(b)'s 0.9% Senior Leverage Ratio cap measured against a $600,000,000 Tangible Net Worth floor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision grants an unrestricted Permitted Discretion right to set reserves and then, two sentences later, promises not to set any reserve absent a Triggering Event — the grant and the promise pull in opposite directions within the same subsection.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10(b) separately lets Lender "set up such reserves against the Borrowing Base or the Maximum Revolver Amount as Lender deems necessary" with no Triggering Event condition, and the parenthetical about liens "specifically identified" on Schedule P-1 as having priority describes a designation Schedule P-1 does not actually make.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second limit — that availability plus cash in the Cash Management Accounts may not exceed Fund's unfunded commitments to makers — is counter-intuitive and its arithmetic purpose is not stated, leaving room for opposed readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with the Borrowing Base, Section 2.4 Overadvances and Section 6.18's requirement to fund subsequent disbursements directly, but no other provision explains the unfunded-commitment cap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence revolving-credit statement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.1(a), 3.4 and 3.6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain and definite, with an express non-exclusive reference to Section 3.3.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.3 does set the conditions precedent to all extensions of credit; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires a written request by noon on the very day of funding, permits telephonic notice "at Lender's election," and then says failure to confirm in writing "shall not affect the validity of the request" — a set of mechanics whose interaction is not obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.8 separately authorises Advances on instructions from "anyone purporting to be an Authorized Person," which is a looser standard than this subsection's requirement of an actual Authorized Person.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite as to timing and destination of funds.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.7 states the same 1:00 p.m. rule in fuller terms; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long, carefully ordered waterfall with defined terms and an internal definition of "paid in full"; the kind of provision that is detailed rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (iv) expressly anticipates and resolves conflicts with other Loan Documents in favour of this Section, which reduces rather than creates whole-instrument risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines "Overadvance" by reference to "any of the limitations set forth in Section 2.1," which includes the opaque unfunded-commitment test in 2.1(c).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.3(b)(D) restrains Lender from an election that would create an Overadvance, and Section 2.1(c) supplies the limits; the chain is consistent but depends on 2.1(c)'s unclear second limb.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-branch rate formula tied to defined terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.12 and the Applicable Margin definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The default rate is set at four points over the rate applicable to Base Rate Loans even for LIBOR Rate Loans, and it applies only "at the election of Lender" without saying how that election is made or communicated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.12(a) lets Lender convert LIBOR loans to Base Rate on default, which partly explains the reference, but the two elections are not linked.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It authorises Lender to charge everything to the Loan Account and to compound unpaid interest into new Advances — commercially aggressive but stated in plain terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The opening carve-out "Except as provided to the contrary in Section 2.10" is loose because Section 2.10 sets several different payment dates; otherwise consistent with Sections 2.9 and 2.5(e).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 360-day convention plus automatic rate adjustment; arithmetically definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Base Rate definition and Section 2.5(e)'s usury savings clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional usury savings clause; its operation is self-executing and expressly retroactive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.10(e) repeats a similar proviso for the minimum interest charge, which is consistent rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and mandatory, but the numbering is garbled and the final sentence imposes a flat 60-day migration to Wells Fargo that the preceding clauses (referring to "one or more" banks on Schedule 2.6) do not anticipate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule 2.6 names Greater Bay Bank and The Mechanics Bank, and Section 2.6(c) lets Administrative Borrower add or replace Cash Management Banks — both hard to reconcile with the requirement that Wells Fargo be the only one after 60 days.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specifies three required terms of the agreements; definite though "among other things" leaves the balance open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.6(e) requires a Cash Management Agreement "with Lender and Borrowers" for Escrow Accounts while this subsection contemplates the bank as a party; a small mismatch in described parties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two different cure periods (30 days for creditworthiness, 60 for performance) keyed to Lender's "reasonable judgment"; detailed and workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The permission to add banks is difficult to reconcile with Section 2.6(a)'s requirement that after 60 days Wells Fargo be the only Cash Management Bank.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, unambiguous lien grant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.1, Borrower Collateral clause (d) and Section 4.7's control requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines "Escrow Account" as a deposit account and then repeatedly refers to "such Cash Management Account," and the carve-out for "accounts belonging to an Account Debtor of Borrower" has no defined boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.17 affirmatively requires deposit into a Lender-lien deposit account of "all amounts delivered to any Borrower to be held on behalf of any Account Debtor," which is the very category this subsection excepts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise conditional-receipt rule with a stated cut-off; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.3(a) and 2.9 and with Schedule L-1's designation of Lender's Account.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It authorises Advances on instructions "from anyone purporting to be an Authorized Person," a striking risk allocation, and the sentence contains a duplicated verb ("agrees to establish establish").

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An account-stated clause with a 30-day objection window and a manifest-error carve-out; standard and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.5(c) and 2.7 and the Lender Expenses definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.5(c) authorises charging "all fees and costs provided for in Section 2.10" to the Loan Account, which supplies the mechanism if not the noun.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The rate is written as "one-half of one percent (0.30%)" — the words and the numeral state two different figures — and the sub-clause labels ("(A)… or (y)") do not match, so the fee cannot be computed from the text alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: This directly contradicts Section 2.12(a)'s automatic conversion to the Base Rate absent a proper exercise of the LIBOR Option — a squarely inconsistent pair of default rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Triggered by Lender's "reasonable opinion" that funding is "unlawful or impractical"; "impractical" is soft but the consequences are spelled out.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the LIBOR Rate and Reserve Percentage definitions.
